summary: Former Devil's Peak station on Eldorado NF's Georgetown district; a 1962 recollection describes Leland Hill's sugar-pine lookout; index lists it gone; county disputed.

facts.design: One-room station building and barn; a tall sugar pine climbed on metal pole steps
facts.status_note: Listed as gone by the Forest Fire Lookout Association; the sources read give no year or cause of removal

events.note: Mountain Democrat and Placerville Times article (January 4, 1962) recalls Leland Hill's early years at the station

evidence.supports: El Dorado County, platform, status Gone, coordinates

evidence.quote: In recalling some of his early experiences Leland Hill said his first year of service at Devil's Peak, on Georgetown district

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Fire Lookout Association index places Devils Peak in El Dorado County at 39.28207, -120.44039; the Forest Lookouts page places Devil's Peak under its Placer County heading and names the Eldorado National Forest. The story uses El Dorado from the index and states the disagreement.

notes_for_editor: One substantive source: a Forest Lookouts page reprinting a 1962 article. No build year appears in it. The index type is Platform, but the article describes a one-room station and a climbed sugar pine, so check before changing the type. The article calls the lookout man Leland Hill and then Bill. Do not confuse this with Signal Peak (Devil's Peak), a staffed tower near Fish Camp, or with Lower Devils Peak in Siskiyou County.
